functional_definition.statement: Asking the person one is talking to for the understanding one is missing -- to have them explain, clarify or restate what they said or meant -- instead of guessing at it or supplying the explanation oneself.
counts_as_realization: the resource's taught production is a request addressed to the interlocutor whose object is the other person's words or meaning (the capability's own face in this repository is "What do you mean by that?", tests/phase3/target_fixtures.py): an explanation, a clarification or a repetition of what was said;
the request is the utterance's own point -- the reveal shows the speaker asking -- rather than a report about asking or about understanding;
the taught ladder puts the speaker in the repair position: something was not understood, the speaker asks the interlocutor about it before going on.
does_not_count: requests for something other than understanding -- an action or an object ("Could you send me the file?", "take a look at this report"), permission ("Could I ask you a question?"), or help ("I was just wondering if you could help me."): asking for these is not asking for a clarification;
expressions that supply a clarification or state that something is understandable ("I mean", "What I'm saying is", "Your plan makes sense");
expressions that name understanding reached by thinking, or that report how something turned out ("figure out", "work out", "turn out");
content vocabulary about attention ("pay attention to"): naming the collocation for focusing on something is not a repair move.
boundary_cases: "I was just wondering if you could help me." is a hedged request for help, not for a clarification of what was said: the object of the request is an action by the hearer, so it does not count.

"Sorry, what does that mean?" (an alternative realization of the capability's own fixture face) asks for the meaning of the other person's words, so it counts -- no resource of the current corpus is of this shape, which is why this node's links are placements at C3-R1.
"Would you mind closing the window?" asks the hearer to act; the frame is a politeness device, not a repair of understanding.
"Could I ask you a question?" is a pre-request: even the question it asks permission for is not yet a clarification, so it does not count.
functional_definition.basis: Authoring judgement made in this repository (C3-R1), read against the canonical vocabulary that actually exists: docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §7's REF family name and §8's expression subtypes, plus this capability's own taught face -- the fixture reveal "What do you mean by that?" whose hint is "Ask the speaker to clarify without repeating them badly" (tests/phase3/target_fixtures.py). No external psychometric or corpus source is claimed. This definition is the standard the §24.7 links into this node were re-reviewed against (curriculum/README.md, C3-R1); it is a declared reading whose Revisit is registered (a canonical definition would supersede it).
